chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: If there are people in a village, they pray the Jumuʿah as four rakʿahs. Then, if they have someone who can deliver the sermon for them, they hold the Jumuʿah when they are five persons. Jumuʿah was only made two rakʿahs because of the two sermons.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ: four units of prayer performed in place of Jumuʿah in the stated circumstance
key_terms.الْخُطْبَتَيْنِ: the two sermons associated with Jumuʿah prayer
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ نَفَرٍ: a group of five persons as the required number mentioned here
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer for Jumuʿah
key_terms.يَخْطُبُ: delivers the sermon to the congregation

ai.seo_question: How many people are needed to establish Jumuʿah prayer in a village, and why is it two rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the performance of Jumuʿah prayer in a village setting. It indicates that when there is a qualified person to deliver the two sermons, a group of five may establish Jumuʿah, and it explains that the prayer was made two rakʿahs in place of the two sermons.
